title: Improved consistency of bond-line thickness when conducting single lap-shear joint tests
author: Flanagan, Byrne, et al.

steps.title: Set up bond‑rig and sample placement
steps.instruction: Place up to ten lap‑shear coupons (101.6 mm long) on the rig, aligning each sample with the +x and –x edges so that the overlap length is 12.7 mm; ensure the top level of the rig is 1.92 mm higher than the bottom level, which together with the coupon thickness (1.62 mm) yields a bond‑line thickness of 0.30 mm (300 µm). This thickness matches the optimal range for 2‑part Scotchweld 2216 epoxy (3 M) and is also suitable for 1‑part Hexcel 300 g/m² Redux 312 film adhesive.

substeps.instruction: Lay out the coupons on the rig, spacing them to accommodate ten samples.
Align the coupons so that the overlap region measures exactly 12.7 mm.
Verify that the rig’s top surface is 1.92 mm above the bottom surface.
Confirm the resulting bond‑line thickness of 0.30 mm using a micrometer or comparable gauge.

steps.title: Apply CoBlast FEP release coating
steps.instruction: Deposit a fluorinated ethylene propylene (FEP) release coating on the contact surfaces of the bond‑rig using the CoBlast process, eliminating the need for the previously used 15 µm non‑stick release film and preventing adhesive over‑fill and film wrinkling during curing.

substeps.instruction: Load the bond‑rig parts into the CoBlast system.
Apply the FEP coating according to the manufacturer’s parameters (as reported for nitinol coatings).
Allow the coating to cure/dry as specified before proceeding to adhesive application.

steps.title: Implement weighted clamping arrangement
steps.instruction: Place calibrated weights uniformly along the y‑direction of the bond‑rig to exert a constant pressure on each bonded sample during the cure cycle, achieving an average bond‑line thickness of 254 µm with less than 10 % variation within any sample.

substeps.instruction: Arrange the weights so that each sample is supported evenly across its length.
Avoid hand‑tightening screws or using the earlier clamping bar with drilled anchor holes.
Start the cure cycle while the weights remain in place, ensuring no shift of the samples.
